QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_19

question.text: Propensity Score Matching (PSM) is a quasi-experimental technique used when:

answer.text: The SIA wants to compute a confidence interval on a binary outcome
The SIA wants to monetise an environmental outcome for SROI
The SIA wants to run a focus-group discussion with beneficiaries
Randomisation is not possible and the SIA constructs a comparison group by matching treated units to untreated units on observable characteristics via a propensity score

explanation.text: The Logic: Propensity Score Matching (PSM) is applied when randomisation is not possible. The SIA constructs a comparison group by matching treated units to untreated units on observable characteristics (gender, age, income, education etc.), summarised as a propensity score (probability of being treated given those covariates). It approximates a randomised comparison using observational data. The Trap: Monetisation is a separate SROI step. Focus groups are qualitative data collection. Confidence intervals are a statistical inference step, not a matching method. Note: The specific Propensity Score Matching concept is not described in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) pages 131-132 or 151, which discuss sampling, confidence interval/margin of error, and qualitative/quantitative/monetisation approaches. The framing above reflects general industry/regulatory knowledge of quasi-experimental impact-evaluation methods.
